transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Could you start by telling me what's been bringing you in today?

I don’t know, it’s like… I just can’t make myself do anything anymore. I mostly sit in my room, and I’ll have the same clothes on for way too long. I used to knit and write in my journal and go walking, like around the neighborhood—there’s this one street with these weird little garden gnomes, I always noticed them—but now I just… don’t. My mom asks me what’s wrong and I barely even have the energy to answer her.
How long has it been since you started feeling this way and losing interest in things like knitting and walking?

I think it started when I began that community college program… which was, um, about two years and two months ago now. It’s weird because I remember buying notebooks for it, like these blue ones that had these little divider tabs, and I thought I was going to be really organized. But around then is when everything just started kind of going downhill, and I stopped caring about the stuff I used to do.
Have you ever had a period, even briefly, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, in contrast to how you've been feeling lately?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like, energetic in a good way or anything. I mean sometimes I stay up, but it’s not because I feel amazing, it’s more like I just get stuck staring at stuff or thinking about random things, like the pattern on my ceiling kind of looks like a map if I look at it too long. But needing less sleep and feeling really happy or powerful or whatever… no, I don’t think I’ve had that.

Over these past two years, has your low mood and lack of interest been present pretty much every day without a break, or have there been stretches—weeks or months—where you felt back to your normal self before it returned?

It’s been kind of… the whole time, I think. Since I started that community college program, like about two years and two months ago. I keep thinking about the first week there because the hallways smelled like cleaning stuff and there were these posters about study skills everywhere, and I remember feeling like I was already behind. But yeah, it’s not like I had some long stretch where I was just normal again. It’s just been this decline since then.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions, or started any new medications or substances, around the time these mood changes began?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I wasn’t like, told I had some new medical thing around then. I don’t remember starting anything new, but my memory about that time is kind of messy. I remember more the college stuff, like the bus route and how I kept missing the same stop because the window had this weird scratch on it I’d stare at. But medications or substances… I don’t think there was anything new like that.
{"int

Sorry, I didn’t catch that—what were you asking? I heard like the start of something, but then I kind of lost it. I do that sometimes when I’m trying to follow the words and then I’m thinking about the sound of the chair or whatever. Could you say it again?
Have you noticed any new problems with your memory, getting confused about where you are, or losing track of time or dates over these past two years?

I don’t know… I mean, I lose track of stuff sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s like dates exactly. My phone tells me the date, so I don’t really have to hold it in my head. Sometimes I’ll walk into a room and forget why, but everybody does that, right?

Getting confused about where I am… not really, I don’t think. Like I know where I am here. The clock in places can mess with me, though, if it’s one of those loud ticking ones, and then I start thinking about how weird it is that seconds are all chopped up like that… sorry. I guess I haven’t noticed some big new memory problem.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight—either eating much more or much less than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I don’t really know. I mean, I eat when there’s food around, mostly. I haven’t been like… keeping track of weight or anything. The scale at home is weird anyway, it has this little crack on the corner and I don’t trust the numbers on it.

But I don’t think there was some big change? Nobody’s said anything to me like that. Sometimes I forget meals or eat random stuff, but I don’t know if that’s different from before.
Over these past two years, has your mood stayed at about the same level the whole time, or was there a period where things got noticeably worse and more intense than your usual baseline?

I’m not really sure. Like, worse compared to what? Because some days feel kind of heavy, but then other days I’m just… normal for me, I guess.

I don’t know if there was one clear period where it suddenly got really intense. I don’t keep track like that. Time sort of blends together, especially when people ask “over two years,” because two years sounds like a hallway, not a number. Sorry. I guess I haven’t noticed a big obvious mood change like that.

During this two-year period, has there ever been a stretch where your low mood was so severe that you had thoughts of death or suicide, or found it nearly impossible to get out of bed or take care of basic needs like eating or bathing?

I don’t… I don’t think I can say yes to that exactly. Like, there are days where I stay in bed too long, but then sometimes it’s because the blankets feel safer or because the room is cold, and then I start thinking about how mornings are kind of fake because the light just changes and everyone decides that means you’re supposed to do things.

But, um… thoughts of death or suicide, I don’t really know. I don’t think I had some clear stretch like you’re saying. And basic stuff… I mean, I’m not great at routines, but I can’t tell if it was “nearly impossible” or just me being bad at doing things on time. I haven’t been tracking it like that.

At any point during these two years, was your low mood and lack of motivation severe enough that it seriously interfered with your ability to attend classes, complete assignments, or maintain relationships with friends or family?

Yeah… I mean, school, yes. That part got messed up. I was doing this certificate program, and it was supposed to lead into a practicum, and then maybe a clinic office job after, like at the front desk or doing the forms—though the forms all look the same to me sometimes, like tiny boxes trying to boss you around.

But I kind of… stopped moving forward with it. I couldn’t handle getting to the practicum part, and planning for the clinic job just became too much. It’s embarrassing because it sounds simple when people say it, like “just finish the program,” but it didn’t feel simple. So yes, it interfered with that.
During this time, have you found yourself feeling unusually worthless, or blaming yourself harshly for things that aren't really your fault?

I don’t know… “worthless” is a big word. I mean, sometimes I feel like I’m not doing things right, or like everyone else got a handbook and I got, I don’t know, a receipt with the ink rubbed off.

But blaming myself for stuff that isn’t my fault… I’m not sure. I do go over things in my head sometimes, like if I said something weird, or if I should’ve answered an email sooner, and then the email becomes this whole object in my mind, like it has weight. But I don’t know if that’s harsh blame exactly.

So… maybe I feel bad about myself sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s unusual or like what you mean.
During this two-year period, have you had trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. My sleep is… weird, but I haven’t been keeping track like, “fell asleep at 2:13” or whatever. Sometimes I’m in bed and it feels like I should be sleeping, but then I start thinking about the ceiling or the little noises in the walls, and then time gets kind of slippery.

But sleeping much more than usual… I don’t know what my usual is supposed to be. In high school it was different because bells told you when to be awake, which is kind of awful but also helpful, I guess. Now it’s less clear.

So, um… maybe there are nights where it’s off, but I can’t say for sure if it’s been a real problem like you’re asking.
During this time, have you noticed it's become harder to concentrate on tasks or make decisions—like when doing schoolwork or everyday things—compared to before?

Um… I’m not sure. I mean, decisions are always kind of annoying, like even picking cereal can turn into this whole thing because the boxes are all yelling different colors at you, and then you think, why are there so many kinds of cinnamon?

But compared to before… I don’t know if I can really measure that. Schoolwork was hard sometimes, but it’s hard to say if that was concentration or just… everything being too much, or me not knowing where to start. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.

So maybe? But I haven’t really noticed it in a clear way.

I guess… I haven’t really noticed it in a way I could point to. Like, sometimes I sit down to do something and then I end up sorting pencils or looking at the same sentence too long, but I don’t know if that’s concentration or just me being me.

Decisions are kind of… I get stuck, but I’ve always gotten stuck. Even with small things, like what shirt to wear, and then I remember this one shirt I had that shrank weird in the wash and it made me mad for like a whole day, which isn’t really what you asked.

So… I don’t know. I can’t clearly say it’s worse than before.

Aside from this steady low mood you've described, has there ever been a period of at least two weeks where your mood or ability to function dropped noticeably below even your usual baseline, then eventually lifted back to how you'd been before that dip?

I’m not sure. Like… two weeks sounds very exact, and I don’t really have my life filed that way. There are times where everything feels lower, I guess, but then it’s hard to tell if it was “below baseline” or just the baseline being bad already.

And “function” is kind of a weird word because I can still do some things, like brush my teeth eventually or move cups from my room to the sink, but then I’ll forget why I went into the kitchen because the light in there is too bright, and then I’m thinking about how kitchens always have that humming sound.

So… I don’t know if there was a separate dip that lifted back up. I can’t really point to one like that.

Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when several of these problems—like sleep changes, appetite changes, trouble concentrating, and low energy—were all happening together and felt more intense than how you'd been feeling generally?

I don’t really know. Like, I can remember stretches where I was sleeping weird or felt drained, but I can’t tell if it all lined up into a two-week chunk like you’re saying.

It’s hard because days sort of run into each other, and then I’ll remember something random, like one week I kept eating toast because it was the only thing that made sense, but I don’t know if that means anything. And concentrating… I mean, sometimes I just stare at stuff, but I don’t know if that was happening with the other things at the same time.

So… maybe there were times it felt heavier, but I can’t really point to a clear period where all of that was together and definitely worse than normal.
